justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modestly constructive but cautious view on the S&P 500 across the three horizons. For the one-day estimate near 2945, I was essentially anchoring close to the prevailing price level, expecting mean-reversion dynamics and relatively thin informational catalysts to keep the index roughly stable in the near term. The one-week estimate of 2960 reflects a slight upward drift consistent with the historical positive drift of equity markets, while acknowledging that short-term momentum and any scheduled data releases could nudge prices higher without dramatically changing the fundamental picture. The one-month estimate of 2990 extends that same logic further, incorporating a modest growth assumption and the idea that, absent a major shock, equities tend to grind higher over a four-week window given supportive monetary conditions that were present at the time of the forecast.

The confidence interval widths were calibrated to grow appropriately with the forecast horizon, reflecting the compounding of uncertainty over time. At the one-day level, the 90% interval of 2880 to 3010 is relatively tight because intraday and overnight dynamics are somewhat mean-reverting and large single-day moves beyond 2–3% are historically rare in the absence of a specific shock. By the one-week window, the interval widens to 2820–3100, incorporating the possibility of a meaningful macro data surprise, a Federal Reserve communication shift, or an escalation in trade policy uncertainty. At the one-month horizon, the interval of 2700–3280 is considerably wider, reflecting the full range of plausible macro outcomes, earnings revisions, and geopolitical developments that could materialize over four weeks.

Several specific risks could push outcomes outside my stated intervals. On the downside, an unexpected deterioration in economic data — such as a sharp rise in unemployment claims, a significant credit event, or an abrupt escalation in geopolitical tensions — could drive the index well below 2700 over a month. A sudden repricing of Federal Reserve expectations toward aggressive tightening would also be a meaningful downside catalyst. On the upside, a comprehensive trade deal announcement, a surprisingly strong earnings season, or an unexpected dovish pivot by the Fed could push the index above 3280. Tail events like a flash crash or a sudden liquidity disruption fall outside the probabilistic mass my intervals are designed to capture, and those remain genuine, if low-probability, risks that no confidence interval fully eliminates.
